The frozen proof supplies its own continuous representative and boundary argument, and the source compatibility statement optimizes unequal radii.

Support inclusion under every anchored representation and projection to the common V-perpendicular space force b_z to be the same convex combination of the b_zi. Each coordinate lies in the anchored representation space. Grouping repeated bases and omitting zero coefficients identifies the assumed positive-weight combinations with the anchored representations of the accepted lift facts.

Completeness of the original stratum activates the canonical congruence fact. An integer graph hull point projects to an original integer site, and each appended coordinate is forced by the associated anchored representation. Projection gives the converse representation map. At m=2 the accepted congruence equivalence preserves the equivalence relation on actual positive sites in the saturated affine lattice, hence exactly k_c.

On a positive-dimensional support, the domination density bound applies to the averages of all intrinsic balls. Compact inner approximation and containment of the sums in the interpolated open ball prove equal-radius root concavity, with positive ball masses at every relative-interior center. Local uniform secant bounds, Arzelà–Ascoli, and weak convergence by Fubini identify the locally uniform limit with the continuous density root. A zero at one relative-interior point forces the nonnegative concave root to vanish everywhere on the interior. The positive support rules this out. The convex support boundary is intrinsically Lebesgue-null and therefore null for the original measure.

The Minkowski sum of small intrinsic balls has an interior ball in the output support because all tangent spaces agree. Testing closed balls of radii εa_i, with weighted average of the a_i equal to one, gives the displayed ε→0 inequality directly for compact positive-mass inputs. If b_i=g_i^(1/r) and T is their weighted sum, substituting a_i=b_i/T gives each term g_i^(1/N)a_i^(q/N)=b_i/T^(q/N), so their weighted sum is T^(r/N). Raising to N/r gives the claimed radius inequality.

The finite limsup extension is upper semicontinuous in the full intrinsic support by the neighborhood-supremum definition. Interior recovery sequences for each input and support compatibility at the averaged output extend the radius inequality to arbitrary boundary inputs, also giving concavity on each support. For q=0, singleton testing gives the same inequality with r=N and the original atom masses.

The radius hypographs in norm form are compact convex sets by upper semicontinuity, compact support, the triangle inequality and concavity. They contain open product neighborhoods because the density is positive and continuous in each support interior, and are positive-radius N-balls when q=0. Offset cancellation and radius compatibility imply every anchored Minkowski inclusion. Grouping all hull points with the same base gives the reverse census inclusion, and all lifted integer fibers are exactly the positive bodies K_z. Their full vertical span and the base affine span give full product dimension after saturated lattice coordinates.

At a fixed base the u-ball volume is ω_r times (fbar/ω_r^(1/r))^r=fbar^r, equal to the intrinsic density almost everywhere and to the full atom mass when q=0. Translation of V onto b_z+V is an isometry. Fubini therefore preserves every Borel mass of the full original stratum law. Choosing a base-lattice basis changes only counting coordinates and contributes no factor to fiber volume. Each physical closed containing halfspace pulls back to a containing closed halfspace or the whole source space, so the depth inequality holds for every physical orientation and every mixed mark.

For the non-hollow case, all positive sites share the same V by the interior-site incidence, and the verified original-base affine offset equals b_z at every site. Original completeness and the same compatibility give exact sections there. If original parities are expressed in that saturated affine lattice, an ambient even difference has its half in the direction space and in the integer lattice, so the parity relation is preserved there too.

Under the stated numerical premise, each exact lifted mixed body is eligible in continuous dimension N at its own saturated integer rank, including rank zero. It has exactly k_c positive occupied parities and total mass W_c, so the transferred mark has physical stratum depth at least Γ_N W_c/k_c. Finite weighted averaging gives a ratio at least W/k(P), and the full measure dominates that selected restriction on every halfspace. A denominator 2 raised to the lifted rank would be a different premise: e.g. a binary cube has no nontrivial anchored representation at any vertex, so its canonical affine rank is 2^n−1 despite the original rank n.
